thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: continuous-batching latency spike in prod-east (p50->p99 cliff), alerting customers. Ticket INC-8921.

maria: I'm on it. seeing huge queue depth on runtime nodes serving model-redwood-v2. p99 latency > 6s, errors rising.

ajay: confirmed. KV cache size exploded on several pods — eviction delayed, OOM margin dropped. suspiciously correlates with a microbatch config change rolled earlier today.

sara: which change? I deployed a batching tweak at 08:04 that increased per-worker microbatch_size from 16->32 to improve throughput for long sequences.

maria: that matches the timeline. at high concurrency that doubled effective KV cache pressure because more partially-filled microbatches kept KV entries alive longer.

jamal: customer impact: several paid customers reported degraded response times and 502 spikes. ops monitoring shows routing retries and some fallback to smaller models. SLA hits likely.

ajay: immediate mitigations proposed: revert microbatch_size to 16, enable temporary eviction throttle, and throttle incoming requests to reduce concurrency for 10m while we rollback.

sara: I can roll back the batch config now. prepping a hotfix release.

maria: while sara rolls back, let's deploy a temporary route policy to divert ~20% traffic to model-redwood-v1 (lower memory) as a safety net. That reduces pressure.

incident-bot: action queue created: INC-8921 -> assign @maria, @sara. on-call escalation at +15m if unresolved.

sara: running rollback:```bash
redwoodctl deploy config set --name microbatch_size --value 16 --target runtime/pool-prod-east
redwoodctl rollout --service runtime --strategy hotfix --wait 300
```

jamal: Please annotate customers in INC-8921 and CC SRE team. I posted an internal note to #customer-impact.

maria: I'm seeing eviction rates climb back down after the first rollback batch completed on 3 nodes. p99 latency trending back toward baseline but still noisy.

ajay: I'm enabling eviction throttle to force more aggressive background evictions as an emergency measure:```yaml
kvcache:
  eviction_policy: aggressive
  background_worker: 4
  eviction_threshold_pct: 60
```

sara: rollout successful on 75% of nodes. one node failed to apply config due to a transient kube scheduling issue, restarting agent.

maria: applying temporary ingress throttle: set concurrency cap per client to 40 for the prod-east route. That should reduce observed queueing.

jamal: customer-facing status: short update sent — "We detected increased latency due to a runtime batching config change; we've deployed a rollback and mitigations; service is recovering. We will follow up with root cause and timeline." :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: postmortem checklist created: assign RCAs, preserve logs (s3://redwood-logs/incidents/INC-8921), capture prometheus snapshots.

ajay: important follow-ups: 1) add safety guard to prevent microbatch_size increases when cluster concurrency > threshold 2) add alert for KV cache growth vs microbatch fill ratio 3) add canary policy to validate KV pressure on config changes.

sara: ack. I'll open PRs for the runtime guard and a preflight check in deploy pipeline.

maria: passing to next on-call for monitoring and handoff. current status: service degraded -> recovering, p99 latency back to ~1.1s from 6s, eviction rates normal, errors dropping.

oncall-next: taking over monitoring. I have the rollback diff and the hotfix command. will keep watch for 30m and escalate if p99 > 2s.

jamal: final note: SLA owners notified, billing/CS looped for impacted customers, and we'll schedule a bridge for tomorrow to run deeper KV cache analysis. Good triage team. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone — saving logs and timeline now. I left a short runbook snippet in INC-8921: how to rollback microbatch + temporary throttles.

incident-bot: thread closed for active paging; on-call handoff complete.
